outline: 886 Finding the Radius Given the Area

examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned} A&=\pi r^{2}\\80&=\pi r^{2}\\r^{2}&=\frac{80}{\pi}\\r&=\pm\sqrt{\frac{80}{\pi}}\end{aligned}$
A radius is positive, so $r\approx5.05\text{ cm}$.

$\begin{aligned} A&=\frac{\pi r^{2}}{2}\\32&=\frac{\pi r^{2}}{2}\\64&=\pi r^{2}\\r^{2}&=\frac{64}{\pi}\\r&=\pm\sqrt{\frac{64}{\pi}}\end{aligned}$
A radius is positive, so $r\approx4.514\text{ m}$.

$\begin{aligned} A&=\frac{\pi r^{2}}{4}\\18&=\frac{\pi r^{2}}{4}\\72&=\pi r^{2}\\r^{2}&=\frac{72}{\pi}\\r&=\pm\sqrt{\frac{72}{\pi}}\end{aligned}$
A radius is positive, so $r\approx4.79\text{ mm}$.

$\begin{aligned} A&=\pi r^{2}\\50&=\pi r^{2}\\r^{2}&=\frac{50}{\pi}\\r&=\pm\sqrt{\frac{50}{\pi}}\end{aligned}$
A radius is positive, so $r=\sqrt{\frac{50}{\pi}}\text{ mm}$.
Double the unrounded radius.
$\begin{aligned} d&=2r\\d&=2\sqrt{\frac{50}{\pi}}\\d&\approx7.98\text{ mm}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned} A&=\frac{\pi r^{2}}{2}\\24&=\frac{\pi r^{2}}{2}\\48&=\pi r^{2}\\r^{2}&=\frac{48}{\pi}\\r&=\pm\sqrt{\frac{48}{\pi}}\end{aligned}$
A radius is positive, so $r=\sqrt{\frac{48}{\pi}}\text{ cm}$.
Double the unrounded radius.
$\begin{aligned} d&=2r\\d&=2\sqrt{\frac{48}{\pi}}\\d&\approx7.82\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned} A&=\frac{\pi r^{2}}{4}\\16\pi&=\frac{\pi r^{2}}{4}\\64\pi&=\pi r^{2}\\r^{2}&=64\\r&=\pm8\end{aligned}$
A radius is positive, so $r=8\text{ cm}$.

$\begin{aligned} A&=\frac{\theta}{360}\pi r^{2}\\27\pi&=\frac{120}{360}\pi r^{2}\\27\pi&=\frac{\pi r^{2}}{3}\\81\pi&=\pi r^{2}\\r^{2}&=81\\r&=\pm9\end{aligned}$
A radius is positive, so $r=9\text{ cm}$.
$\begin{aligned} d&=2r\\d&=2\times9\\d&=18\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned} A&=\frac{\theta}{360}\pi r^{2}\\48\pi&=\frac{\theta}{360}\pi(8)^{2}\\17280\pi&=64\pi\theta\\\theta&=\frac{17280\pi}{64\pi}\\\theta&=270^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
This is the reflex interior angle of the sector.

The outer radius is $R=24\div2=12\text{ cm}$.
$\begin{aligned} A&=\pi R^{2}-\pi r^{2}\\80\pi&=\pi(12)^{2}-\pi r^{2}\\\pi r^{2}&=144\pi-80\pi\\\pi r^{2}&=64\pi\\r^{2}&=64\\r&=\pm8\end{aligned}$
A radius is positive, so $r=8\text{ cm}$.
$\begin{aligned} d&=2r\\d&=2\times8\\d&=16\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

coverage.summary: Authored nine worked examples covering every distinct retained assessment method, with separate editable prompts and solutions and changed source values. Working follows formula, substitution and inverse operations; independent equations retain full left-hand sides and need no phantom equals. Solution prose and mathematics inherit the renderer's blue. Native diagrams use black outlines and ordinary labels declared at 10 pt; the ring alone uses purposeful standard light-blue shading. examples.derivation: 80 = πr² gives r = √(80/π) ≈ 5.046265 cm, hence 5.05 cm. Reject the negative root because the radius is positive.
32 = πr²/2 gives r² = 64/π and positive r ≈ 4.513517 m, hence 4.514 m. The centre-to-endpoint portion of the diameter labelled r is a radius.
18 = πr²/4 gives r² = 72/π and positive r ≈ 4.787307 mm, hence 4.79 mm. The diagram shows a quadrant and its right angle.
50 = πr² gives positive r = √(50/π) mm. Therefore d = 2√(50/π) ≈ 7.978846 mm, hence 7.98 mm, without intermediate rounding.
24 = πr²/2 gives positive r = √(48/π) cm. Therefore d = 2√(48/π) ≈ 7.817640 cm, hence 7.82 cm.
16π = πr²/4 gives 64π = πr², so r² = 64 and the positive radius is exactly 8 cm.
27π = (120/360)πr² = πr²/3 gives r² = 81. The positive radius is 9 cm and the diameter is 18 cm. The diagram explicitly marks the given 120° sector.
48π = (θ/360)π(8)² gives 17280π = 64πθ and θ = 270°. The outer arc and angle mark both trace the reflex interior angle.

The outer radius is 12 cm. From 80π = 144π − πr², obtain r² = 64 and positive r = 8 cm, so the inner diameter is 16 cm. Diagram radii 1.8 and 1.2 have the correct 12:8 ratio; shading identifies the given ring area.
